title: Cybersecurity for IT Teams
subtitle: Understand the threats and put the essential defences in place
audience_line: System and network administrators, support staff and IT managers
overview: This programme gives IT teams the security knowledge they need in their daily work. Participants learn how attackers operate, then secure networks, Windows and Linux endpoints, access and data, run the basic security operations that make ransomware survivable, and respond to an incident following NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3. They finish with governance: policies, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST CSF 2.0, GDPR and the Tunisian personal data protection law. Every chapter ends with a lab or exercise, and the programme closes with a final project in which teams assess a small company and present a hardening plan.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: System and network administrators, support staff and IT managers

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None in security. Day-to-day IT administration experience (users, networks, Windows or Linux) is expected

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 27 h: 24 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by labs and exercises on realistic company scenarios

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant (16 GB RAM) with Windows Server evaluation and Linux virtual machines and a pfSense firewall, prepared by the trainer; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab or exercise validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can recognise common attacks, harden networks, endpoints and access, prepare backups and a first incident response, and map controls to ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF

phases.name: Threats & Network Security
phases.focus: Threat actors, kill chain, common attacks, segmentation, firewalls, wireless
phases.intro: Participants learn who attacks, how an attack unfolds and which techniques are most common, from phishing to network and application attacks, then reduce the network attack surface with segmentation, firewall rules and secure wireless. Validated lab: a segmented network on pfSense where only the allowed flows pass between users, servers and guests.

chapters.title: Threat Landscape & Attacks
chapters.content: Threat actors, kill chain, malware, phishing and social engineering, network and application attacks

phases.name: Endpoints & Access
phases.focus: Windows and Linux hardening, patching, EDR, MFA, least privilege, encryption, PKI
phases.intro: Participants harden Windows and Linux machines and keep them patched, see what endpoint detection and response adds, then control access with MFA and least privilege and protect data with encryption and certificates. Validated lab: a Windows and a Linux server hardened against a checklist, with administrative access limited and logged.

chapters.title: Securing Endpoints
chapters.content: Windows and Linux hardening, patching, EDR

chapters.title: Access & Cryptography
chapters.content: MFA, least privilege, encryption, PKI basics

phases.name: Operations, Response & Governance
phases.focus: Logs and alerts, backups and ransomware, incident response, policies and standards
phases.intro: Participants collect the logs and alerts that matter and build backups that survive ransomware, respond to an incident with the NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 approach, then frame security as governance: policies, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST CSF 2.0, GDPR, Tunisian Organic Law 2004-63 and security culture. Validated exercise: a ransomware tabletop exercise worked through by each team, with the restore tested.

chapters.title: Security Operations
chapters.content: Logs, alerts, backups and ransomware resilience

chapters.title: Incident Response
chapters.content: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, first response, communication

chapters.title: Governance & Risk
chapters.content: Policies, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST CSF 2.0, GDPR and Tunisian Organic Law 2004-63, security culture

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A security assessment and hardening plan for a small company
phases.intro: Teams of two or three assess the security of a small company described in a written brief and its lab network, reusing the phase labs, then present a hardening plan as they would to its management.

chapters.title: Brief & Assessment
chapters.content: Read the brief, inventory assets, identify risks, check the lab network against the controls of the course

chapters.title: Plan & Policies
chapters.content: Prioritised controls, key policies, incident response checklist

chapters.title: Presentation & Review
chapters.content: Present the plan to the group as to management; questions and feedback

project.title: Security Assessment of a Small Company
project.brief: A small company assessed from its brief and lab network: risks, prioritised controls mapped to ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF, key policies and an incident response checklist, presented as a hardening plan.
project.stack: pfSense, Windows Server, Linux, risk register, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and NIST CSF 2.0 references
project.deliverable: Risk register, hardening plan, policies, incident response checklist, presentation
